question: Two pipes A and B can fill the tank in 40 and 60 minutes, respectively. Both the pipes are opened together. After how many minutes should the pipe B be turned off, so that the tank be fill in 30 minutes?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let **Total Capacity** of the tank be **LCM(40, 60) = 120 units**.

**Efficiency of A** = 120 ÷ 40 = 3 units/min | **Efficiency of B** = 120 ÷ 60 = 2 units/min.

Pipe A remains open for the full **30 minutes**, filling 3 × 30 = 90 units.

Remaining work (120 − 90 = 30 units) is done by **Pipe B**.

Time for Pipe B = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** Pipe A fills in 40 min, Pipe B fills in 60 min, Total time = 30 min.

**Formula Used:** Total Work = Time × Efficiency.

⇒ Total capacity = 120 units.

⇒ Work done by **Pipe A** in 30 minutes = 30 × 3 = 90 units.

⇒ Remaining work to be done by **Pipe B** = 120 − 90 = 30 units.

⇒ Time for which Pipe B was open = 30 ÷ 2 = 15 minutes.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 min.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Pipes and Cisterns Concept

If a pipe can fill a tank in x hours and another can empty it in y hours, the net part filled in 1 hour = (1/x − 1/y) where y > x.

Work and Wages

Wages are always distributed in the ratio of the **Efficiency** of the workers or the ratio of **Work Done** by them.

Alternate Day Work

In alternate work problems, calculate the work done in one **cycle** (sum of efficiencies) and then find the number of cycles required.</p
